newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Repairs to troubled Mir delayed again.
newsitem.headline: Repairs to troubled Mir delayed again.

text.p: Russian space officials on Monday decided to delay vital repairs to the Mir space station, scheduled for Wednesday, by two or three days because of a new energy supply problem, a senior Mission Control official said.

"With this computer fault today we are bracing ourselves for a tense situation with the battery buffers, our energy reserves," flight director Vladimir Solovyov told reporters. "Unfortunately we have to move back repairs by two or three days."
The decision to delay followed a redocking between Mir and its Progress resupply ship on Monday, an operation which was switched at the last minute to manual rather than automatic pilot.
The main computer on the Mir station also suffered some kind of failure, sending the station spinning in disorientation, Solovyov said.
Mir, which draws its energy from keeping its solar panels aimed at the sun, would probably stay disorientated until at least Tuesday morning, he said.
"It will be chaotically spinning," he said. "We have turned off all energy-consuming equipment and only left life support systems operational."
